title: Cellular innovations and diversity in the lepidopteran compound eye
note: Full review, figure captions and figures read. Supplementary Table S1 inspected: it inventories opsin gene copies, which are not measured photoreceptor-class counts and were not recast as such. Secondary measurements retain their primary-study attribution in each note.

title: The scaling of eye size with body mass in birds
note: Complete eight-page paper read from Europe PMC PDF service. Table 1 and scaling analyses measure or estimate eye dimensions/mass, skull dimensions and body mass. They do not give measured acuity, visual-field width, spectral sensitivity, flicker fusion or other numeric traits in BRIEF. Scaling-based predictions were not logged as measured acuity.

title: Ultra-rapid vision in birds
note: Whole paper and free supplements read: S1 Table supplies 75 individual FFF measurements. Main text reports mean CFFs 130.3, 128.1, 138.2 Hz, while the abstract reports 129, 127, 137 Hz; raw S1 data agree with the main text. ERG secondary results retain their separate method.

title: Night light-adaptation strategies for photosynthetic apparatus in yellow-poplar (Liriodendron tulipifera L.) exposed to artificial night lighting
note: Complete 25-page paper read, including figure captions; no supplemental files listed. Records describe experimentally measured nonvisual physiological responses to HPS night lighting, not photoreceptor spectra or visual thresholds. Numerical graph values were not guessed from plots; reported prose values retain exposure, time and response endpoint.

title: Praying mantises possess multiple spectral photoreceptor classes
note: Whole paper and Table 1 read. Females only; ERG recorded from dorsal region and supports physiological/model class differences, not behavioural colour discrimination. Public Figshare raw-data link was followed; retrieval outcomes are summarized in the progress note.

title: Spectral Sensitivity Studies on the Visual System of the Praying Mantis, Tenodera sinensis
note: Complete 20-page scanned paper read from Europe PMC PDF service. The XML contains an abstract, a PDF-only notice and selected references, and was not treated as full text. The ocellus supports at least two receptor types; the compound-eye experiment did not establish additional classes and explicitly does not exclude them.

title: Metabolic rate and body size are linked with perception of temporal information
note: Whole paper including Tables 1-2, appendix Tables A1-A9 and figure captions read. Table 1 supplies 34 secondary species-specific CFF values, with ERG/behavioural and optimum/suboptimum codes retained. Environmental H/L classification was not recast as stimulus luminance; mass/metabolism/brain-size regressions were not logged as measured sensory traits.
